_meta.note: System materials are Apple-defined blur levels. The Liquid Glass numeric budgets below are NOT all Apple-published numbers — several come from independent accessibility audits and Figma's Glass effect. Provenance is tagged per rule. Treat 'community-bestpractice' as guardrails to confirm, not gospel.
_meta.verify_against: HIG > Foundations > Materials; WWDC 'Meet Liquid Glass'; current Xcode SwiftUI glass APIs

system_materials.guidance: Pick a level by how much background should read through. Heavier material = more legible foreground, less depth. Use vibrancy for text/symbols on top of materials.

apple_guidance.rule: Apple publishes NO numeric blur-radius cap or layer count. The stated rule is qualitative: reserve Liquid Glass for the navigation layer (bars, controls, sheets), not main content; let content scroll behind it. The numeric budgets below are community/Figma heuristics to confirm, NOT Apple values.
apple_guidance.verify_against: HIG > Foundations > Materials; WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass'

control_depth_max.note: Figma Glass 'Depth' >20 harms readability for UI controls

frost_range.note: Figma Glass 'Frost'; >30 reads as milky plastic

min_text_contrast.when: measured AFTER blur against the actual backdrop

over_photo.rule: Custom .glassEffect loses the 4.5:1 contrast guarantee over a busy or high-contrast photo. When the backdrop is photographic: (a) prefer a heavier system material (thickMaterial / chromeMaterial) behind text instead of custom glass, OR (b) lay a legibility scrim between photo and text — a linear gradient from .clear to a semantic background/fill (e.g. Color(.systemBackground)) over the text band — then re-measure contrast AFTER blur. Never rely on glass alone for legibility over imagery.

fallback.rule: Ship a solid (or near-solid ~20% opacity over solid) variant and swap at runtime. Never rely on translucency for legibility.

lift_tip.note: Keep text/symbols on a layer ABOVE the glass group; a subtle inner light (white ~30%, blur ~6) helps separation.
